title: Moroccan Chicken and Chickpeas
seoTitle: Moroccan Chicken and Chickpeas | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Warm-spiced thighs with chickpeas, apricots, and roasted carrots
subtitle: Warm-spiced thighs with chickpeas, apricots, and roasted carrots
description: Chicken thighs roast with chickpeas, carrots, dried apricots, and ras el hanout-inspired spices until fragrant and caramelized.

steps.title: Mix spice blend
steps.instruction: Combine cumin, cinnamon, ginger, paprika, garlic, salt, and olive oil into a paste that coats a spoon without separating.

steps.title: Coat chicken and vegetables
steps.instruction: Toss thighs, chickpeas, carrots, onion, and apricots with spice paste until every piece looks evenly coated and lightly glossy.

steps.title: Roast until chicken is done
steps.instruction: Spread on two half-sheets in a single layer. Roast at 425°F 32–38 minutes until chicken reads 165°F and chickpeas crisp at edges.

steps.title: Rest and check texture
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Apricots should be plump and lightly caramelized; carrots tender with slight bite at the center.

steps.title: Serve with couscous
steps.instruction: Portion chicken with chickpea mixture. Pan should smell warm-spiced, not burnt; chicken juices should run clear.

proTips: Ras el hanout blend works if you have it—use 2 tbsp instead of individual spices.
Offer harissa at the line for heat without changing the base tray.
Couscous cooks in 5 minutes—ideal side while tray rests.
tonightSpread: Plain Greek yogurt for cooling contrast.
leftovers: Moroccan grain bowl with leftover couscous and chickpeas.
Shred chicken into a wrap with hummus spread.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Adventurous flavor without exotic equipment. Sweet apricots balance warm spices for broad crew appeal.
mealPrepNotes: Mix spice blend in bulk for future trays. Soak apricots 10 minutes if very dry. Station: Drain and pat chickpeas dry—they crisp better when not dripping. Station: Use two pans so chickpeas roast instead of steam under crowded chicken. Station: Scatter fresh cilantro at the line, not before hold—herbs wilt in hot pans.
